title: Goal
description: One level of the results hierarchy (TAXONOMY.md D25): a goal (the long-term aim) has no parent, an objective (a specific aim) has a goal as its parent, and an outcome (a changed state) has an objective as its parent. Every other component references a goal record instead; a goal record never references a lower component. The kind keeps the name Goal as an identifier for all three levels.

parent.description: Required for objectives and outcomes; forbidden for a goal. An objective or outcome may be left unplaced while what it sits under is not defined yet, with a placeholder holding this field's place (metadata.pending, TAXONOMY.md D35); it is listed as unplaced until placed.

objective.description: The goal as Cartograph states it: one glanceable sentence naming the desired future state. Where the goal comes from a published plan, this is the reading, and statedAs is the record.

statedAs.description: The goal exactly as its source states it, unaltered, where that source is a published plan or policy. Uncapped in practice because plan prose is not written to fit a field; objective carries the short reading beside it. Never paraphrase into this property.

source.description: Where statedAs was taken from, precisely enough to find again: the document, and the section or page.

owner.description: The role accountable for this aim, from the Resource catalogue, never a person (GPRA's goal leader; the programme sponsor's counterpart for an aim). Optional; a check asks for one.

horizon.description: When work on this aim starts and when it should be reached, as a year or a year and month. Optional below a goal: an objective or outcome without one takes its parent's. Time-bound (SMART) reads targets against it, and a check flags a horizon that runs past its parent's (TAXONOMY.md D26).

goal.description: A higher objective this outcome also leads to, beyond the one it is filed under.

because.description: Why this outcome leads to that objective, written so somebody could disagree with it.

contributesTo.description: The objectives this outcome leads to, besides its parent, each with the reason (results-based management's contribution, a theory of change's 'because'). parent files a goal in one place; contributesTo says what else it serves and why, so one outcome can feed objectives under different goals. Outcomes only (a kind rule advised by the checks). See TAXONOMY.md D24.
